Hi there! Formerly worked at a corporate tire retailer. They have 3 levels of technicians. General Service Technicians handle basic tasks like tire changes and oil changes, while General Maintenance Technicians perform more extensive maintenance tasks and assist when the main Technicians are busy. Technicians handle all other services and may also take on some General Maintenance work during slower periods.

General Service and General Maintenance Technicians are paid hourly based on clocked time, while Technicians are compensated on a flat rate basis. The flat rate is determined by the customer's payment, and service contracts often pay a lower rate. This allows the company to secure contracts and profit from larger accounts. Consequently, a 3-hour job on a company vehicle does not pay the same as a 3-hour job on a personal vehicle. As a result, Technicians often prefer to pass these larger accounts to General Maintenance Technicians when they have other tasks to complete. I can confirm this from my experience as both a General Maintenance Technician and a Technician.

Technicians also have a guarantee of 75% of their clocked hours. This means that if they work 40 hours in a week, they are guaranteed to be paid for 30 hours. If they only clock 25 hours, they still receive payment for 30 hours. If they work 35 hours, they are paid for 35 hours, with no additional conditions.

So, you can be assured that it didn't negatively impact that individual's paycheck at a corporate tire retailer. At least, that was my experience from about 6 years ago, and I believe all corporate stores operate in a similar manner.
